title: Honesty
competency: Explain honesty and its importance, and behave honestly.

keywords.def: Not telling or accepting lies, not stealing or cheating; being truthful in what you say and do.

en.text: Moral virtues let us live well in our community. Honesty is being truthful in what we say and do: not telling or accepting lies, not stealing or cheating. Honest people are trusted and respected; dishonesty and corruption destroy trust and harm development.

screens.title: Figure 1.2: the lost wallet
screens.ask: A boy finds a wallet full of money and runs after the owner to give it back. Why might he do that?
screens.after: Returning what is not yours is honesty. Everyone respects a truthful person.

screens.title: Moral virtues
paras: Virtue ethics has two categories: moral virtues and civic virtues.
Moral virtues are dispositions that let a person live reasonably in the community, according to their values.

screens.title: Honesty
paras: Being truthful in what you say and do is honesty.
It means not telling or accepting lies, and not stealing or cheating.
Honest people are loyal to their fellows, their responsibility and their country.
Being called honest is one of the best compliments a person can receive.
screens.note: Dishonesty with public property is corruption. Corruption wastes resources and harms progress and development.

screens.title: The African fable: Truth, Falsehood, Water and Fire
steps: Four travellers found four cattle and agreed to share equally.
Greedy Falsehood lied to Water that Fire would burn his land.
Water believed him and put Fire out.
Falsehood then tricked Truth too. When Truth found out, they fought.
Wind could not decide who owned the cattle. Lies destroyed trust and caused conflict.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Not telling or accepting lies, not stealing or cheating; being truthful in what you say and do.

screens.text: Which is a consequence of dishonesty?
opts: It erodes trust among friends and the community
screens.ans: It erodes trust among friends and the community
screens.why: Dishonesty destroys trust; honesty earns respect.

screens.text: In the fable, what was wrong with Water?
opts: He believed a lie without checking and acted violently
screens.ans: He believed a lie without checking and acted violently
screens.why: Honesty includes not accepting lies; Water should have found the truth first.

screens.text: The best policy is honesty, the habit of telling the truth.

screens.why: Abusing public property is dishonest; responsible citizens fight corruption.

screens.text: In an exam, Abel sees the answer sheet left on the desk. No one would ever know if he looked. What would an honest person do and why?
opts: Not look, because honesty is truthfulness even when no one watches
Look but share with no one
screens.ans: Not look, because honesty is truthfulness even when no one watches
screens.why: Honesty means not cheating. It comes from character, not from fear of being caught.
screens.clue: Is honesty only for when people are watching?

items.text: What is the significance of honesty?

test.text: A lack of honesty is a way to disaster.
